title: Why Characteristic 0 is Essential
content: The module header sets up the goal — the power sums generate the full symmetric subalgebra — over the ground field ℚ. The characteristic-0 hypothesis is not cosmetic: it is exactly what makes the statement true. Newton's identities express each elementary symmetric polynomial eₖ as a ℚ-polynomial in the power sums p₁,…,pₖ, but the recursion divides by k (e.g. e₂ = (p₁² − p₂)/2, e₃ = (p₁³ − 3p₁p₂ + 2p₃)/6). Over a field of characteristic p ≤ n these divisions fail, and the power sums no longer generate: the eₖ can escape the subalgebra they span. Working over ℚ (characteristic 0) all the denominators are invertible, so the reverse Newton identities hold and the two subalgebras coincide.
mathContext: Newton: $k\,e_k = \sum_{i=1}^{k}(-1)^{i-1}e_{k-i}p_i$; solving for $e_k$ needs $k^{-1}$, available iff $\operatorname{char} = 0$ (or $>n$).
prerequisites: Newton's identities relating pₖ and eₖ
why division by k requires characteristic 0

title: The Subalgebra Generated by the Power Sums (over ℚ)
content: `psumAdjoin σ := Algebra.adjoin ℚ (Set.range (psum σ ℚ))` is the smallest ℚ-subalgebra of `MvPolynomial σ ℚ` containing every power sum `pₙ`. Here the base ring is fixed to **ℚ** (not a general ℚ-algebra as in the parent), because the whole point of this entry is to compare it with `symmetricSubalgebra σ ℚ` — both must be subalgebras over the *same* ground field for `le_antisymm` to produce an honest equality of objects of the same type.
prerequisites: why both subalgebras need the same ground ring

title: Easy Inclusion: Power Sums Are Symmetric
content: `psumAdjoin_le_symmetric` proves `psumAdjoin σ ≤ symmetricSubalgebra σ ℚ`. By `Algebra.adjoin_le` it suffices that every *generator* lies in the symmetric subalgebra; the generators are the power sums `psum σ ℚ n`, each symmetric by `psum_isSymmetric`. Since `symmetricSubalgebra` is closed under the algebra operations, the entire generated subalgebra is contained in it. This direction uses no characteristic-0 input — it holds over any base.
mathContext: $A \le \mathrm{symmetricSubalgebra}\,\sigma\,\mathbb{Q}$ because each $p_n$ is symmetric and the symmetric polynomials form a subalgebra.

title: Hard Inclusion: Fundamental Theorem ∘ Reverse Newton
content:
`symmetric_le_psumAdjoin` is the genuine synthesis. Fix a symmetric `p` and set `n = |σ|`.

1. **Fundamental theorem.** `esymmAlgHom_surjective` (with `n ≥ |σ|`, here equality via `le_rfl`) gives `q` with `esymmAlgHom σ ℚ n q = ⟨p, hp⟩`. Taking `.val` and rewriting by `esymmAlgHom_apply` yields `aeval (fun i ↦ esymm σ ℚ (i+1)) q = p` — `p` is a ℚ-polynomial in `e₁,…,eₙ`.
2. **adjoin = range of aeval.** `Algebra.adjoin_range_eq_range_aeval` identifies `(aeval f).range` with `Algebra.adjoin ℚ (Set.range f)`, so the witness `⟨q, hpval⟩` proves `p ∈ adjoin ℚ {e₁,…,eₙ}`.
3. **Reverse Newton.** `Algebra.adjoin_le` reduces `adjoin ℚ {eₖ} ≤ psumAdjoin` to membership of each generator `esymm σ ℚ (i+1)`, supplied verbatim by the parent's `esymm_mem_adjoin_psum σ ℚ (i+1)`.

The composition `symmetric ⟹ poly in eₖ ⟹ poly in pₖ` is what upgrades the parent's membership statement to a generation statement.
prerequisites: eₖ ∈ adjoin of power sums (parent result)

title: Equality and the Membership Corollary
content: `psum_adjoin_eq_symmetric` assembles the two inclusions with `le_antisymm`, giving the headline `Algebra.adjoin ℚ (Set.range (psum σ ℚ)) = symmetricSubalgebra σ ℚ`: the power sums generate *exactly* the symmetric subalgebra. `isSymmetric_mem_psumAdjoin` restates the hard direction in concrete membership form — any symmetric polynomial over ℚ is a ℚ-polynomial in the power sums — by feeding `IsSymmetric` through `mem_symmetricSubalgebra` into `symmetric_le_psumAdjoin`.
